review.title: Nhận xét bài viết trên lớp
paragraphs: Nowadays, some people think that school should reward students who show the best academic results, while others believe that it is more important to reward students who show improvements.

On the one hand, rewarding for students who have the best achievements is very necessary. First, students who have diligently applied themselves to their study, they deserve their praises and privileges, this may encourage those students and others to study harder to win the rewards and propel towards overall academic gains. Second, this kind of competition we would see in almost every aspect of life, where only the best individuals are rewarded. Students are used to this reality and thrive in the face of fierce competition and enable them to achieve success in later life.

On the back hand, students who show improvements also should have rewards. Initially, only a few smart students can come first and receive the rewards, cause others to think that their effort is futile. Because they can not surpass those outstanding individuals and prone to feeling overwhelmed and disheartened and lose the incentive to study. Furthermore, emphasizing improvements encourage all students to be diligent in their student also help students to understand that they need to constantly improve themselves, irrespective of how well they have been or are performing. The constant desire to outdo themselves, even benefits themselves more than the competitive determination to win against all others.
review.overall: Em triển khai được đủ hai thân bài và có nhiều ý đúng của dàn ý. Tuy nhiên, bài thiếu ý kiến cá nhân ở mở bài và thiếu kết bài; nhiều câu cũng đang bị nối bằng dấu phẩy hoặc thiếu động từ chính. Em cần viết lại để nêu rõ trường học nên thưởng cả hai nhóm và hoàn chỉnh từng mắt xích lập luận.

paragraphs: Opinions are divided over whether schools should reward academic excellence or give greater recognition to students who make progress. I believe that both groups should receive rewards.

Admittedly, rewarding students who achieve the best academic results is justified. Since they have diligently applied themselves to their studies, they deserve their praises and privileges. This may encourage them and other students to study harder to win rewards, which may lead to overall academic gains. Furthermore, competition is seen in almost every aspect of life, where only the best individuals are rewarded. Students can become used to this reality and thrive in the face of fierce competition, which may enable them to achieve success in later life.

However, students who show progress should also be rewarded. If only a few high-achieving students receive rewards, other students may feel that further effort is futile because they cannot surpass those outstanding individuals. As a result, they may feel overwhelmed and disheartened and lose the incentive to study. Furthermore, emphasizing improvements encourages all students to be diligent in their studies and helps them understand that they need to keep improving themselves, irrespective of their current performance. The constant desire to outdo themselves may benefit students more than the determination to defeat others.
In conclusion, schools should reward both students who achieve the best academic results and those who make progress.
